author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Existing vet feature package and patterns cover the slice (system-design § Package Structure, § Contracts; architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog: Repository, Value object, Web controller). Adjustment: two new contracts in `vet` -- `SpecialtyRepository` (read-only lookup repository, precedent `PetTypeRepository`) and `SpecialtyDirectory` (immutable value object holding the grouping and ordering rule, so the controller holds no business rule) -- plus a `GET /specialties.html` handler on `VetController`. Design-doc writes: Contracts rows for REQ-VET-003, one invariant sentence fixing the stable order the PRD left open (specialties by name; holders by last name, then first name; identity breaks ties), and a new § Scale and Load section with the specialty-directory row. Covering code resolved by grep (IDE oracle not connected; weaker basis): `Vet.getSpecialties`, `VetRepository.findAll()` @Cacheable("vets"), `PetTypeRepository.findPetTypes` ORDER BY name, layout fragment `layout (template, menu)`.
integration_points: Entry point GET /specialties.html on VetController binds no request data: no @RequestParam, no @ModelAttribute, no form object; the binding target is none. Unknown query parameters are ignored, and no persisted type is bound (security-principles § Trust Boundaries; the id-disallow binder rule is not needed because nothing binds).

Handler reads `SpecialtyRepository` (every specialty, including unheld ones) and the cached `VetRepository.findAll()`, builds `SpecialtyDirectory` from both, adds it to the model, and returns the `vets/specialtyList` view. No pagination and no page parameter (REQ-VET-003 vs REQ-VET-001's paged `/vets.html`, which is untouched).

Double, domain unit (SpecialtyDirectoryTests): real `Vet` and `Specialty` instances, no doubles -- this test carries edge cases 1-3 and the omission of veterinarians holding no specialty (testing-principles minimal-mocking).

Double, repository boundary in the web-slice test (VetControllerTests, @WebMvcTest + MockMvc, the sanctioned transport stand-in): framework stub @MockitoBean for `SpecialtyRepository`, alongside the file's existing @MockitoBean `VetRepository`. Reason: @WebMvcTest excludes JPA repositories, and this file's fixture already stubs `VetRepository` this way. The rules under test live in `SpecialtyDirectory`, so the stubs only feed rendering. No other stub is sanctioned.

Double, persistence boundary: the real repository over embedded H2 via the existing @DataJpaTest `ClinicServiceTests`, if a query test is added for `SpecialtyRepository` returning every seeded specialty. No double.

View: `vets/specialtyList.html` uses `fragments/layout :: layout(~{::body}, <menu>)` with a menu value matching no existing entry, so the shared navigation renders unchanged and gains no entry (REQ-SYS-001). Every label uses a message key present in all 11 bundles; specialty and veterinarian names render as stored via escaped th:text (REQ-LANG-002; the existing I18nPropertiesSyncTest and template walk enforce this).

template shape: layout fragment, #{key} labels, table of names, th:each over specialties
Value object row: immutable, equal by value, defensive copies. SpecialtyDirectory carries values (names), not references to the mutable persistence entities

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Widened surface stated and minimal: the one new route `@GetMapping("/specialties.html")` (VetController.java, `showSpecialtyDirectory(Model model)`) is a read-only GET taking no request parameter, path variable, or bound object, so no external input crosses the boundary and no @ModelAttribute/@RequestBody mass-assignment target is introduced.

XSS: specialtyList.html renders every data value through escaping `th:text` (`th:text="${entry.specialtyName}"`, `th:text="${holder}"`); `grep -rn -F -e 'utext' -e '__$' src/main/resources/templates/` shows no th:utext and no preprocessing in the new template, and its layout call passes the literal menu key 'specialties', not request data.

Data access: SpecialtyRepository extends Spring Data `Repository<Specialty, Integer>` with a single derived `findAll()` marked `@Transactional(readOnly = true)`; there is no query text, so no injection surface and no write path (least privilege).

Resource bounds: the unpaged full read matches the existing unpaged `vetRepository.findAll()` behind `/vets` (VetController `showResourcesVetList`), and the PRD requires a single page; system-design Scale and Load records the data set as bounded with no in-app write path, so this change adds no new unbounded-allocation vector.

Lazy loading under open-in-view=false: Vet.java:47 `@ManyToMany(fetch = FetchType.EAGER)` means grouping reads `getSpecialties()` without a LazyInitializationException, so the error page cannot leak an exception message.

No secrets, logging, file I/O, process execution, or deserialization in the diff (the full `python3 scripts/changeset.py` output was read); SpecialtyDirectory is an immutable record built with List.copyOf and holds no shared mutable state.

Supply chain: build.gradle is not in the change set (the changeset file list has no build file), so no dependency was added. build.gradle has no dependencyCheckAnalyze plugin (`grep -i dependencycheck build.gradle` found nothing), so no NVD match ran in this review. `./gradlew dependencies` resolves Spring Boot 4.1.1, jackson-databind 3.1.5 and Thymeleaf 3.1.5.RELEASE.
